Enum.description: Address/Data MUX mode (ADMUX)
Enum.name: AM_0

Enum.description: Address/Data non-MUX mode (Non-ADMUX)
Enum.name: AM_1

Enum.description: ADV# is active low.
Enum.name: ADVP_0

Enum.description: ADV# is active high.
Enum.name: ADVP_1

Enum.description: AHB bus timeout counter is not enabled.
Enum.name: BTOEN_0

Enum.description: AHB bus timeout counter is enabled.
Enum.name: BTOEN_1

Enum.description: Internal clock gating is enabled, that means the function clock is off when no access.
Enum.name: CG_EN

Enum.description: Internal clock gating is disabled, that means the function clock is always on.
Enum.name: CG_DIS

Enum.description: No reset.
Enum.name: NO_RST

Enum.description: Assert reset.
Enum.name: RST

Enum.description: All the SRAMC registers are allowed to write.
Enum.name: LOCK_0

Enum.description: All the SRAMC registers are not allowed to write except Lock register.
Enum.name: LOCK_1

Enum.description: SRAM access does not need to monitor wait pin.
Enum.name: WEN_0

Enum.description: SRAM access need to monitor wait pin.
Enum.name: WEN_1

Enum.description: Wait signal is determined by level of wait pin.
Enum.name: WS_0

Enum.description: Wait signal is determined by both conditions of wait pin level and internal wait counter. Quits wait state when both of them exit waiting.
Enum.name: WS_1

Enum.description: Wait signal is determined by any condition of wait pin level and internal wait counter. Quits wait state when any of them exits waiting.
Enum.name: WS_2

Enum.description: Wait signal is determined by edge of wait pin.
Enum.name: WS_4

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: Normal mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFPINx]. If neither FHALF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. The PWM outputs disabled by this fault input will not be re-enabled until the actual FAULTx input signal de-asserts since the fault input will combinationally disable the PWM outputs (as programmed in DISMAPn).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Safe mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear and FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FHLAF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: SAFE

Enum.description: Manual fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. This is further controlled by FCTRL[FSAFE].
Enum.name: MANUAL

Enum.description: Automatic fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are enabled when FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFLAGx]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: Normal mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFPINx]. If neither FHALF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. The PWM outputs disabled by this fault input will not be re-enabled until the actual FAULTx input signal de-asserts since the fault input will combinationally disable the PWM outputs (as programmed in DISMAPn).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Safe mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear and FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FHLAF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: SAFE

Enum.description: Manual fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. This is further controlled by FCTRL[FSAFE].
Enum.name: MANUAL

Enum.description: Automatic fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are enabled when FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFLAGx]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: Normal mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFPINx]. If neither FHALF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. The PWM outputs disabled by this fault input will not be re-enabled until the actual FAULTx input signal de-asserts since the fault input will combinationally disable the PWM outputs (as programmed in DISMAPn).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Safe mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear and FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FHLAF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: SAFE

Enum.description: Manual fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. This is further controlled by FCTRL[FSAFE].
Enum.name: MANUAL

Enum.description: Automatic fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are enabled when FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFLAGx]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: FAULTx CPU interrupt requests disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: FAULTx CPU interrupt requests enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Normal mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFPINx]. If neither FHALF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. The PWM outputs disabled by this fault input will not be re-enabled until the actual FAULTx input signal de-asserts since the fault input will combinationally disable the PWM outputs (as programmed in DISMAPn).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Safe mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear and FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FHLAF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: SAFE

Enum.description: Manual fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. This is further controlled by FCTRL[FSAFE].
Enum.name: MANUAL

Enum.description: Automatic fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are enabled when FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFLAGx]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: No loading action taken. Users can write new values to buffered registers (writing into outer-set of these buffered registers)
Enum.name: LDOK0

Enum.description: Outer-set values are ready to be loaded into inner-set and take effect. The loading time point depends on CTRL2[LDMOD].
Enum.name: LDOK1

Enum.description: DMA is disabled
Enum.name: DMAEN_0

Enum.description: DMA is enabled. DMA request asserts automatically when the values in the outer-set of buffered compare registers (UCOMP0/LCOMP0;UCOMP1/LCOMP1;UCOMP2/LCOMP2;UCOMP3/LCOMP3), initial registers(UINIT/LINIT) and modulus registers (UMOD/LMOD) are loaded into the inner-set of buffer and then LDOK is cleared automatically. After the completion of this DMA transfer, LDOK is set automatically, it ensures outer-set values can be loaded into inner-set which in turn triggers DMA again.
Enum.name: DMAEN_1

Enum.description: No Watchdog timeout interrupt has occurred
Enum.name: WDIRQ0

Enum.description: Watchdog timeout interrupt has occurred
Enum.name: WDIRQ1

Enum.name: XNE0

Enum.name: XNE1

Enum.name: XIRQ0

Enum.description: INDEX/PRESET pulse has occurred
Enum.name: XIRQ1

Enum.description: Standard quadrature decoder, where PHASEA and PHASEB represent a two-phase quadrature signal.
Enum.name: PH10

Enum.description: Single phase mode, bypass the quadrature decoder, refer to CTRL2[CMODE] description
Enum.name: PH11

Enum.description: Count normally and the position counter initialization uses upper/lower initialization register UINIT/LINIT
Enum.name: REV0

Enum.description: Count in the reverse direction and the position counter initialization uses upper/lower modulus register UMOD/LMOD
Enum.name: REV1

BitField.name: SWIP

Enum.description: No action
Enum.name: SWIP0

Enum.description: Initialize position counter
Enum.name: SWIP1

BitField.description: Use Negative Edge of HOME/ENABLE Input
BitField.name: HNE

Enum.description: When CTRL[OPMODE] = 0,use HOME positive edge to trigger initialization of position counters. When CTRL[OPMODE] = 1,use ENABLE high level to enable POS/POSD/WDG/REV counters
Enum.name: HNE0

Enum.description: When CTRL[OPMODE] = 0,use HOME negative edge to trigger initialization of position counters. When CTRL[OPMODE] = 1,use ENABLE low level to enable POS/POSD/WDG/REV counters
Enum.name: HNE1

BitField.description: Enable HOME to Initialize Position Counter UPOS/LPOS
BitField.name: HIP

Enum.description: No action
Enum.name: HIP0

Enum.description: HOME signal initializes the position counter
Enum.name: HIP1

Enum.description: No transition on the HOME/ENABLE signal has occurred
Enum.name: HIRQ0

Enum.description: A transition on the HOME/ENABLE signal has occurred
Enum.name: HIRQ1

Enum.description: Decode Mode: Input nodes INDEX/PRESET and HOME/ENABLE are assigned to function of INDEX and HOME.
Enum.name: OPMODE0

Enum.description: Count Mode: Input nodes INDEX/PRESET and HOME/ENABLE are assigned to functions of PRESET and ENABLE. In this mode: (1)only when ENABLE=1, all counters (position/position difference/revolution/watchdog) can run, when ENABLE=0, all counters (position/position difference/revolution/watchdog) can't run. (2) the rising edge of PRESET input can initialize position/revolution/watchdog counters (position counter initialization also need referring to bit CTRL[REV]).
Enum.name: OPMODE1

Enum.description: Buffered registers are loaded and take effect immediately upon CTRL[LDOK] is set.
Enum.name: LDMOD0

Enum.description: Buffered registers are loaded and take effect at the next roll-over or roll-under if CTRL[LDOK] is set.
Enum.name: LDMOD1

Enum.description: Use INDEX pulse to increment/decrement revolution counter (REV)
Enum.name: REVMOD0

Enum.description: Use modulus counting roll-over/under to increment/decrement revolution counter (REV)
Enum.name: REVMOD1

Enum.description: POS_MATCH[x](x range is 0-3) is asserted when the Position Counter is equal to according compare value (UCOMPx/LCOMPx)(x range is 0-3), and de-asserted when the Position Counter not equal to the compare value (UCOMPx/LCOMPx)(x range is 0-3)
Enum.name: OUTCTL0

Enum.description: All POS_MATCH[x](x range is 0-3) are asserted a pulse, when the UPOS, LPOS, REV, or POSD registers are read
Enum.name: OUTCTL1

Enum.description: Period measurement functions are not used. POSD is loaded to POSDH and then cleared whenever POSD, UPOS, LPOS or REV is read.
Enum.name: PMEN0

Enum.description: Period measurement functions are used. POSD is loaded into POSDH and then cleared only when POSD is read.
Enum.name: PMEN1

BitField.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.
BitField.name: TIME_STAMP

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.
BitField.name: DLC

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.
BitField.name: IDE

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.
BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.
BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.name: ESI

BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: STD

BitField.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.
BitField.name: PRIO

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

BitField.name: PRIO

BitField.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.
BitField.name: TIME_STAMP

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.
BitField.name: DLC

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: STD

BitField.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.
BitField.name: DLC

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.
BitField.name: IDE

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.
BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.
BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

BitField.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.
BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.
BitField.name: DLC

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.
BitField.name: IDE

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.
BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.
BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: STD

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: STD

BitField.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.
BitField.name: PRIO

BitField.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.
BitField.name: TIME_STAMP

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.
BitField.name: DLC

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.
BitField.name: IDE

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.
BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.
BitField.name: DLC

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: STD

BitField.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.
BitField.name: PRIO

BitField.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.
BitField.name: TIME_STAMP

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.
BitField.name: DLC

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.
BitField.name: IDE

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.
BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.
BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.name: SRR

BitField.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.
BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.
BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.
BitField.name: TIME_STAMP

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.
BitField.name: DLC

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

Enum.name: SET_OFLAG

Enum.name: TOGGLE_OFLAG_SUCCESS

Enum.name: TOGGLE_OFLAG_ALT

Enum.description: Set on compare, cleared on secondary source input edge
Enum.name: CLEAR_ON_SECONDARY

Enum.description: Set on compare, cleared on counter rollover
Enum.name: CLEAR_ON_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Enable gated clock output while counter is active
Enum.name: ENABLE_GATED_OUT

Enum.description: Co-channel counter/timers cannot force a re-initialization of this counter/timer
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Co-channel counter/timers may force a re-initialization of this counter/timer
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Count up.
Enum.name: COUNTUP

Enum.description: Count down.
Enum.name: COUNTDOWN

Enum.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and then continue by re-initializing the counter from the LOAD register.
Enum.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count repeatedly.
Enum.name: REPEAT

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count down.

Enum.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and then continue by re-initializing the counter from the LOAD register.
Enum.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count repeatedly.
Enum.name: REPEAT

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count repeatedly.
Enum.name: REPEAT

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: The external pin is configured as an input.

Enum.name: OFLAG_OUT

Enum.description: True polarity.
Enum.name: TRUE

Enum.description: Inverted polarity.
Enum.name: INVERTED

Enum.description: Capture function is disabled
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Load capture register on rising edge (when IPS=0) or falling edge (when IPS=1) of input
Enum.name: ENABLE_RISING

Enum.description: Load capture register on falling edge (when IPS=0) or rising edge (when IPS=1) of input
Enum.name: ENABLE_FALLING

Enum.description: Load capture register on both edges of input
Enum.name: ENABLE_BOTH

Enum.name: COUNTER_ACTIVE

Enum.description: Clear OFLAG output on successful compare
Enum.name: CLEAR_OFLAG

Enum.description: Set OFLAG output on successful compare
Enum.name: SET_OFLAG

Enum.description: Toggle OFLAG output on successful compare
Enum.name: TOGGLE_OFLAG_SUCCESS

Enum.description: Toggle OFLAG output using alternating compare registers
Enum.name: TOGGLE_OFLAG_ALT

Enum.description: Set on compare, cleared on secondary source input edge
Enum.name: CLEAR_ON_SECONDARY

Enum.description: Set on compare, cleared on counter rollover
Enum.name: CLEAR_ON_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Enable gated clock output while counter is active
Enum.name: ENABLE_GATED_OUT

Enum.description: Co-channel counter/timers cannot force a re-initialization of this counter/timer
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Co-channel counter/timers may force a re-initialization of this counter/timer
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Count up.
Enum.name: COUNTUP

Enum.description: Count down.
Enum.name: COUNTDOWN

Enum.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and then continue by re-initializing the counter from the LOAD register.
Enum.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count repeatedly.
Enum.name: REPEAT

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.name: INACTIVE

BitField.description: Excessive Deferral When the DTXSTS bit is set in the MAC_OPERATION_MODE register and the DC bit is set in the MAC_CONFIGURATION register, this bit indicates that the transmission ended because of excessive deferral of over 24,288 bit times (155,680 in 1000/2500 Mbps mode or when Jumbo packet is enabled).

Enum.name: INACTIVE

Enum.description: Excessive deferral
Enum.name: ACTIVE

BitField.description: Late Collision When the DTXSTS bit is set in the MAC_OPERATION_MODE register, this bit indicates that the packet transmission aborted because a collision occurred after the collision window (64 bytes including Preamble in MII mode; 512 bytes including Preamble and Carrier Extension in GMII mode).

Enum.name: INACTIVE

Enum.description: Late collision is sensed
Enum.name: ACTIVE

BitField.description: Excessive Collisions When the DTXSTS bit is set in the MAC_OPERATION_MODE register, this bit indicates that the transmission aborted after 16 successive collisions while attempting to transmit the current packet.
BitField.name: EXCOL

Enum.description: No collision
Enum.name: INACTIVE

Enum.description: Excessive collision is sensed
Enum.name: ACTIVE

BitField.description: CSR Clock Range The CSR Clock Range selection determines the frequency of the MDC clock according to the CSR clock frequency used in your design: - 0000: CSR clock = 60-100 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/42 - 0001: CSR clock = 100-150 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/62 - 0010: CSR clock = 20-35 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/16 - 0011: CSR clock = 35-60 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/26 - 0100: CSR clock = 150-250 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/102 - 0101: CSR clock = 250-300 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/124 - 0110: CSR clock = 300-500 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/204 - 0111: CSR clock = 500-800 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/324 The suggested range of CSR clock frequency applicable for each value (when Bit 11 = 0) ensures that the MDC clock is approximately between 1.

BitField.description: Address Enable When this bit is set, the Address filter module uses the 64th MAC address for perfect filtering.
BitField.name: AE

Enum.description: Address is ignored
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Address is enabled
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: MAC ADDRESS63 [31:0] This field contains the lower 32 bits of the 64th 6-byte MAC address.
BitField.name: ADDRLO

BitField.description: Counters Reset When this bit is set, all counters are reset.
BitField.name: CNTRST

Enum.description: Counters are not reset
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: All counters are reset
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Counter Stop Rollover When this bit is set, the counter does not roll over to zero after reaching the maximum value.
BitField.name: CNTSTOPRO

Enum.description: Counter Stop Rollover is disabled
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Counter Stop Rollover is enabled
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Reset on Read When this bit is set, the MMC counters are reset to zero after Read (self-clearing after reset).
BitField.name: RSTONRD

Enum.description: Reset on Read is disabled
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Reset on Read is enabled
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: MMC Counter Freeze When this bit is set, it freezes all MMC counters to their current value.
BitField.name: CNTFREEZ

Enum.description: MMC Counter Freeze is disabled
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: MMC Counter Freeze is enabled
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Counters Preset When this bit is set, all counters are initialized or preset to almost full or almost half according to the CNTPRSTLVL bit.
BitField.name: CNTPRST

Enum.description: Counters Preset is disabled
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Counters Preset is enabled
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Full-Half Preset When this bit is low and the CNTPRST bit is set, all MMC counters get preset to almost-half value.
BitField.name: CNTPRSTLVL

Enum.description: Full-Half Preset is disabled
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Full-Half Preset is enabled
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Update MMC Counters for Dropped Broadcast Packets Note: The CNTRST bit has a higher priority than the CNTPRST bit.
BitField.name: UCDBC

Enum.description: Update MMC Counters for Dropped Broadcast Packets is disabled
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Update MMC Counters for Dropped Broadcast Packets is enabled
Enum.name: ENABLE

Register.description: Tx Packets Aborted By Underflow Error
Register.name: MAC_TX_UNDERFLOW_ERROR_PACKETS

BitField.description: Tx Underflow Error Packets This field indicates the number of packets aborted because of packets underflow error.
BitField.name: TXUNDRFLW

BitField.description: Tx Single Collision Good Packets This field indicates the number of successfully transmitted packets after a single collision in the half-duplex mode.
BitField.name: TXSNGLCOLG

BitField.description: Tx Multiple Collision Good Packets This field indicates the number of successfully transmitted packets after multiple collisions in the half-duplex mode.
BitField.name: TXMULTCOLG

BitField.description: Tx Deferred Packets This field indicates the number of successfully transmitted after a deferral in the half-duplex mode.
BitField.name: TXDEFRD

BitField.description: Tx Late Collision Packets This field indicates the number of packets aborted because of late collision error.
BitField.name: TXLATECOL

BitField.name: TXEXSCOL

BitField.description: Tx Carrier Error Packets This field indicates the number of packets aborted because of carrier sense error (no carrier or loss of carrier).
BitField.name: TXCARR

BitField.description: Tx Octet Count Good This field indicates the number of bytes transmitted, exclusive of preamble, only in good packets.
BitField.name: TXOCTG

BitField.description: Tx Packet Count Good This field indicates the number of good packets transmitted.
BitField.name: TXPKTG

Register.description: Packets Aborted By Excessive Deferral Error
Register.name: MAC_TX_EXCESSIVE_DEFERRAL_ERROR

BitField.name: TXEXSDEF

BitField.description: Tx Pause Packets This field indicates the number of good Pause packets transmitted.
BitField.name: TXPAUSE

BitField.description: Tx VLAN Packets Good This field provides the number of good VLAN packets transmitted.

BitField.description: Rx Multicast Packets Good This field indicates the number of good multicast packets received.
BitField.name: RXMCASTG

BitField.description: Rx CRC Error Packets This field indicates the number of packets received with CRC error.
BitField.name: RXCRCERR

BitField.description: Rx Alignment Error Packets This field indicates the number of packets received with alignment (dribble) error.
BitField.name: RXALGNERR

BitField.description: Rx Runt Error Packets This field indicates the number of packets received with runt (length less than 64 bytes and CRC error) error.
BitField.name: RXRUNTERR

BitField.name: RXJABERR

BitField.name: RXUNDERSZG

BitField.description: Rx Out of Range Type Packet This field indicates the number of packets received with length field not equal to the valid packet size (greater than 1,500 but less than 1,536).
BitField.name: RXOUTOFRNG

BitField.description: Rx Pause Packets This field indicates the number of good and valid Pause packets received.
BitField.name: RXPAUSEPKT

Register.description: Missed Packets Due to FIFO Overflow

BitField.description: Rx FIFO Overflow Packets This field indicates the number of missed received packets because of FIFO overflow.
BitField.name: RXFIFOOVFL

Register.description: Good and Bad VLAN Packets Received

BitField.description: Rx VLAN Packets Good Bad This field indicates the number of good and bad VLAN packets received.
BitField.name: RXVLANPKTGB

BitField.description: Rx Watchdog Error Packets This field indicates the number of packets received with error because of watchdog timeout error (packets with a data load larger than 2,048 bytes (when JE and WD bits are reset in MAC_CONFIGURATION register), 10,240 bytes (when JE bit is set and WD bit is reset in MAC_CONFIGURATION register), 16,384 bytes (when WD bit is set in MAC_CONFIGURATION register) or the value programmed in the MAC_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT register).
BitField.name: RXWDGERR

BitField.description: Rx Receive Error Packets This field indicates the number of packets received with Receive error or Packet Extension error on the GMII or MII interface.
BitField.name: RXRCVERR

BitField.description: Rx Control Packets Good This field indicates the number of good control packets received.
BitField.name: RXCTRLG

BitField.description: Tx LPI Microseconds Counter This field indicates the number of microseconds Tx LPI is asserted.
BitField.name: TXLPIUSC

Register.description: Number of Times Tx LPI Asserted
Register.name: MAC_TX_LPI_TRAN_CNTR

BitField.description: Tx LPI Transition counter This field indicates the number of times Tx LPI Entry has occurred.
BitField.name: TXLPITRC

BitField.description: Rx LPI Microseconds Counter This field indicates the number of microseconds Rx LPI is asserted.
BitField.name: RXLPIUSC

Register.description: Number of Times Rx LPI Entered

BitField.name: RXLPITRC

Enum.description: Abnormal Interrupt Summary status detected

BitField.description: Normal Interrupt Summary Normal Interrupt Summary bit value is the logical OR of the following bits when the corresponding interrupt bits are enabled in the DMA_CH0_INTERRUPT_ENABLE register: - Bit 0: Transmit Interrupt - Bit 2: Transmit Buffer Unavailable - Bit 6: Receive Interrupt - Bit 11: Early Receive Interrupt Only unmasked bits (interrupts for which interrupt enable is set in INTERRUPT_ENABLE register) affect the Normal Interrupt Summary bit.
BitField.name: NIS

BitField.description: Abnormal Interrupt Summary Abnormal Interrupt Summary bit value is the logical OR of the following when the corresponding interrupt bits are enabled in the INTERRUPT_ENABLE register: - Bit 1: Transmit Process Stopped - Bit 7: Receive Buffer Unavailable - Bit 8: Receive Process Stopped - Bit 10: Early Transmit Interrupt - Bit 12: Fatal Bus Error - Bit 13: Context Descriptor Error Only unmasked bits affect the Abnormal Interrupt Summary bit.
BitField.name: AIS

Enum.description: Abnormal Interrupt Summary status not detected
Enum.name: INACTIVE

Enum.description: Abnormal Interrupt Summary status detected
Enum.name: ACTIVE

BitField.description: Normal Interrupt Summary Normal Interrupt Summary bit value is the logical OR of the following bits when the corresponding interrupt bits are enabled in the INTERRUPT_ENABLE register: - Bit 0: Transmit Interrupt - Bit 2: Transmit Buffer Unavailable - Bit 6: Receive Interrupt - Bit 11: Early Receive Interrupt Only unmasked bits (interrupts for which interrupt enable is set in INTERRUPT_ENABLE register) affect the Normal Interrupt Summary bit.
BitField.name: NIS

Enum.description: Normal Interrupt Summary status not detected
Enum.name: INACTIVE

Enum.description: Normal Interrupt Summary status detected
Enum.name: ACTIVE

BitField.description: Enable Slot Comparison When set, this bit enables the checking of the slot numbers programmed in the Tx descriptor with the current reference given in the RSN field.

Enum.description: Slot Comparison is disabled
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Slot Comparison is enabled

BitField.description: Advance Slot Check When set, this bit enables the DMA to fetch the data from the buffer when the slot number (SLOTNUM) programmed in the Tx descriptor is - equal to the reference slot number given in the RSN field or - ahead of the reference slot number by up to two slots This bit is applicable only when the ESC bit is set.

Enum.description: Advance Slot Check is enabled
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Indicates to the transmit data FIFO that the written frames contain two additional octets before the frame data. This means the actual frame begins at bit 16 of the first word written into the FIFO. This function allows putting the frame payload on a 32-bit boundary in memory, as the 14-byte Ethernet header is extended to a 16-byte header.
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.description: Enables insertion of IP header checksum.
BitField.name: IPCHK

Enum.description: Checksum is not inserted.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: If an IP frame is transmitted, the checksum is inserted automatically. The IP header checksum field must be cleared. If a non-IP frame is transmitted the frame is not modified.
Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: Checksum not inserted.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: If an IP frame with a known protocol is transmitted, the checksum is inserted automatically into the frame. The checksum field must be cleared. The other frames are not modified.
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.description: Enable Padding Removal For Short IP Frames
BitField.name: PADREM

Enum.description: Padding not removed.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: Any bytes following the IP payload section of the frame are removed from the frame.
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.description: Enable Discard Of Frames With Wrong IPv4 Header Checksum
BitField.name: IPDIS

Enum.description: Frames with wrong IPv4 header checksum are not discarded.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: If an IPv4 frame is received with a mismatching header checksum, the frame is discarded. IPv6 has no header checksum and is not affected by this setting. Discarding is only available when the RX FIFO operates in store and forward mode (RSFL cleared).
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.description: Enable Discard Of Frames With Wrong Protocol Checksum
BitField.name: PRODIS

Enum.description: Frames with wrong checksum are not discarded.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: If a TCP/IP, UDP/IP, or ICMP/IP frame is received that has a wrong TCP, UDP, or ICMP checksum, the frame is discarded. Discarding is only available when the RX FIFO operates in store and forward mode (RSFL cleared).
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.description: Enable Discard Of Frames With MAC Layer Errors
BitField.name: LINEDIS

Enum.description: Frames with errors are not discarded.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: Any frame received with a CRC, length, or PHY error is automatically discarded and not forwarded to the user application interface.
Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: Instructs the MAC to write two additional bytes in front of each frame received into the RX FIFO.
Enum.name: ONE

Register.name: RCMR1

Enum.description: Disabled (default): no compares will occur and the classification indicator for this class will never assert.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: The register contents are valid and a comparison with all compare values is done when a VLAN frame is received.
Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: The DMA controller's channel for the class is not used. Disabling the DMA controller of a class also requires disabling the class match comparator for the class (see registers RCMRn). When class 1 and class 2 queues are disabled then their frames will be placed in queue 0.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: Enable the DMA controller to support the corresponding descriptor ring for this class of traffic.
Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: The traffic shaper function should consider 12 octets of IPG in addition to the frame data transferred for a frame when doing bandwidth calculations. This is the default.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: Addition of 12 bytes for the IPG should be omitted when calculating the bandwidth (for traffic shaping, when writing a frame into the transmit FIFO, the shaper will usually consider 12 bytes of IPG for every frame as part of the bandwidth allocated by the frame. This addition can be suppressed, meaning short frames will become more bandwidth than large frames due to the relation of data to IPG overhead).
Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: The DMA controller's channel for the class is not used. Disabling the DMA controller of a class also requires disabling the class match comparator for the class (see registers RCMRn). When class 1 and class 2 queues are disabled then their frames will be placed in queue 0.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: Enable the DMA controller to support the corresponding descriptor ring for this class of traffic.

Enum.description: The traffic shaper function should consider 12 octets of IPG in addition to the frame data transferred for a frame when doing bandwidth calculations. This is the default.

Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: The timer stops at the current value.

Enum.description: The timer can be reset to zero when the given offset time is reached (offset event). The field is cleared when the offset event is reached, so no further event occurs until the field is set again. The timer offset value must be set before setting this field.

Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: A period event interrupt can be generated (EIR[TS_TIMER]) and the event signal output is asserted when the timer wraps around according to the periodic setting ATPER. Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: No results to report.

Enum.description: Attached to an SDP. Must comply with USB 2.0 by drawing only 2.5 mA (max) until connected.
Enum.name: CONN_SDP

Enum.description: Attached to a charging port. The exact meaning depends on the STATUS[SEQ_STAT] field (value 0: Attached to either a CDP or a DCP. The charger type detection has not completed. value 1: Attached to a CDP. The charger type detection has completed.)
Enum.name: CONN_CP

Enum.description: Attached to a DCP.
Enum.name: CONN_DCP

Enum.description: The module is either not enabled, or the module is enabled but the data pins have not yet been detected.
Enum.name: NO_DATA_PIN_CONN

Enum.description: Data pin contact detection is complete.
Enum.name: DATA_PIN_CONN

Enum.description: Charging port detection is complete.
Enum.name: CP_DET_DONE

Enum.description: Charger type detection is complete.
Enum.name: CT_DET_DONE

Enum.description: No sequence errors.
Enum.name: NO_SEQ_ERR

Enum.description: Error in the detection sequence.
Enum.name: SEQ_ERR

Enum.description: The detection sequence is not running for over 1 s.
Enum.name: NO_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: It is over 1 s since the data pin contact was detected and debounced.
Enum.name: TIMEOUT

Enum.description: The sequence is not running.
Enum.name: SEQ_NOT_RUNNING

Enum.description: The sequence is running.
Enum.name: SEQ_RUNNING
